bio.text: For the last thirty years of his life he worked in secret melancholy at the pictures and drawings that were his real self — those very pictures and drawings that now are prized beyond the whole range of his satirical and comic work.

source.author: Michael Sadleir
source.title: Daumier: The Man and the Artist

bio.text: [Daumier’s] drawing is fluent and easy; it is a continuous improvisation. He has a wonderful, almost super-human memory, from which he works as from a model.
bio.lead: Charles Baudelaire, his friend and neighbour on the Île Saint-Louis:

source.author: Charles Baudelaire
source.title: Curiosités esthétiques (1868), trans. Helen Chisholm in Henri Frantz, Daumier (The Studio, 1904), as quoted on Wikiquote

bio.text: He earned a living producing caricatures and cartoons in newspapers and periodicals such as La Caricature and Le Charivari, for which he became well known in his lifetime and is still remembered today.
